data.name: Kshanansh
data.gender_notes: Kshanansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Kshanansh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kshana', meaning 'moment' or 'instant'. In Hindu mythology, the god of time is called 'Kala' and the term 'Kshana' refers to a single moment in time. The name signifies the divine moment, the present, and the importance of cherishing every second of life. The name Kshanansh carries the meaning “Divine moment, instant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kshanansh usually hope their child will grow to embody divine moment, instant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the present moment, cherish every second of life.
data.etymology: Kshanansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Divine moment, instant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kshanansh total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kshanansh holds a deep cultural significance in the Hindu tradition. The name presents a connection to the god of time, affirming the importance of each passing moment. The term 'Kshana' is mentioned in numerous Hindu scriptures and holds a respectable place in Indian culture. Additionally, in various regional traditional practices, naming a child Kshanansh fosters a sense of appreciation for the divine moment and the journey of life.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Kshanansh carries immense significance. It is a constant reminder of the fleeting nature of time and the importance of cherishing each moment of life. The name is a spiritual connection to the divine, encouraging the bearer to live mindfully and presently. It also serves as a reminder of the interconnectedness of all things, encouraging individuals to spread love and compassion to all beings in every moment. The name inspires individuals to live in the present, make the most of each moment, and tap into their spiritual potential, making Kshanansh a profoundly meaningful name.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kshanansh: In Hinduism, 'Kshan' represents a moment or an instant in time, while 'Ansh' means essence or part. Hence, Kshanansh signifies one who embodies the essence of the present moment.

historical_references.reference: The Kshatrapas were a dynasty of Indo-Scythian rulers that emerged in the western part of ancient India in the late 1st century BC. They were originally vassals of the Indo-Greek kings and later became independent. The Kshatrapas ruled over present-day Gujarat and parts of Malwa, Rajasthan and Saurashtra. The name 'Kshatrapa' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Kshatra-Pati', meaning 'Lord of the Army'.
